title: Prospective signal curation and buyers' heuristic index for model procurement
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Produce a reproducible index (Buyer Heuristic Index, BHI) that synthesizes competitive signals about open and provider models to help Redwood procurement and GTM decide which model variants to onboard, reserve capacity for, or avoid. This ticket scopes data collection, scoring rules, prototype dashboard, and a short playbook for using the index in procurement decisions.

Background: We frequently get ad-hoc requests from Sales and Solutions to validate whether a model is 'enterprise-ready' (latency, uptime, compliance, quantization compatibility). Meanwhile Procurement asks for a fast, defensible way to prioritize reserved capacity purchases. This index is intended to be the single, small-number summary used in RFx reviews and early procurement gating.

Scope and deliverables: 1) Signal taxonomy and weight recommendations (latency profile, empirical uptime, quantization/ops compatibility, licensing friction, on-prem compatibility, vendor lock risk, community adoption velocity, security/compliance flags). 2) Data pipeline spec: sources (public benchmarks, telemetry samples from hosted customers, partner telemetry, vendor SLAs, GitHub/issue velocity, downstream breakage signals). 3) Scoring rubric and example scores for 30 candidate model variants (including top open models and Redwood-verified variants). 4) Prototype BHI dashboard (table + radar view) and a CSV export used by Procurement. 5) Short playbook (1-pager) describing how Sales/PMs should interpret BHI buckets (Green/Amber/Red).

Constraints and assumptions: - We will only use aggregated telemetry (no customer PII). - Early version uses coarse TTL windows (7/30/90 day) for velocity signals. - This is aimed at procurement & GTM; the index intentionally trades off model nuance for a single-signal decision heuristic.

Success criteria: adoption by Procurement in at least one RFx within 6 weeks; sample of 30 models scored and checked into repo; prototype dashboard linked from Console backlog; documented rubric and owners for signal refresh cadence (weekly).
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy doc checked into /docs/procurement-bhi (Confluence link in comments)
Pipeline spec in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/model-bhi (initial README + cron), dataset export (CSV) attached
Scoring rubric published and reviewed by Procurement and Research (>=2 signoffs)
Prototype dashboard deployed on staging (table + radar) and accessible to procurement team
Playbook 1-pager written and approved by Head of GTM
comments: 2026-03-06 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket and initial hypothesis. Rationale: Procurement wants a compact, repeatable signal for buying decisions. Linked examples from vendor scorecards.

2026-03-08 - Ethan Zhao: Quick intake meeting notes: prioritize signals we can compute automatically from public sources + Redwood telemetry. Blocker: need legal sign-off on using aggregated partner telemetry; added dependency on LEG-212.

2026-03-09 - Research (Lina Park): Ran quick survey with 12 enterprise buyers (summary in Drive: drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BHI-survey). Key finding: buyers weight predictable latency and upgrade stability > peak throughput for procurement decisions.

2026-03-10 - Engineering (Rohit Singh): Proto pipeline: github.com/redwood-inference/model-bhi/tree/proto. Pull request PR#142 contains ingestion for public SLAs and GitHub issue velocity. Notes in PR about rate limits and caching.
2026-03-11 - Procurement (Maya Chen): Suggest adding 'contract flexibility' as a negative score factor (ease of exit). Added to the taxonomy draft.

2026-03-12 - PM review (Ava Martinez): Adjusted weights: latency 25%, uptime 20%, op-compatibility 15%, license friction 15%, vendor lock risk 10%, adoption velocity 10%, compliance flags 5%. Rationale documented in Confluence page.

2026-03-13 - Design (Jonah Lee): Proposed dashboard wireframes uploaded: drive.google.com/file/d/1BHI-wireframes. Feedback: include per-model historical trend sparkline for BHI and separate breakdown view for the top 3 contributing signals.
2026-03-14 - Legal (Priya Nair): Confirmed aggregated telemetry use OK if no customer identifiers persist. LEG-212 closed. Suggest adding retention policy (90 days) — added to pipeline spec.

2026-03-15 - Product leadership (Clara Ruiz): Requested pilot with Procurement for two live RFx decisions in April. Action: prioritize scoring the 30 candidate models (list in comments) and deploy staging dashboard by 2026-03-28.

Links and artifacts: Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/BHI-Procurement, GitHub proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-bhi, Wireframes: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BHI-wireframes, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-bhi/pull/142, Staging dashboard: https://staging.console.redwood-inference.com/bhi (placeholder)
Risks & trade-offs: We sacrifice per-workload nuance for shotgun decision-making. Need to state clearly on playbook that BHI is a procurement filter not a final technical acceptance test.
Next steps: - Finish ingestion for telemetry and license signals (ENG-assignments created). - Score initial 30 models and run QA. - Deploy staging dashboard and invite Procurement to pilot.
